summary: Advance your organisational social media strategy, governance, and analytics in 5 intensive days. Enrol your team today.
lede: Social Media Management for Organisations helps you coordinate channels, content, paid media, communities, and reporting around clear business objectives. Over five days, you work with the PESO model, OKR goal setting, social media funnel design, UTM-based attribution, and channel-specific playbooks to build a more consistent operating system. You will practise auditing social activity, creating a RACI governance matrix, planning content and asset workflows, configuring dashboards, and building an analytics scorecard. The course also introduces AI-assisted content operations, crisis simulation, and advanced attribution concepts while addressing budget limits, approval processes, compliance review, stakeholder expectations, and ongoing platform changes.
audienceIntro: This training is built for professionals who already manage organisational social channels and now need to scale governance, impact, and reporting across multiple brands, markets, or business units.
modules: Enterprise Social Media Strategy and Governance
Social Media Audit and Competitor Benchmarking
Advanced Content Strategy and Calendar Design
Paid Social, Targeting, and Budget Allocation
Community Management, Influencers, and Social Care
Crisis Management and Reputational Risk on Social
Global, Multi-Brand, and Cross-Functional Social Operations
AI, Automation, and Scalable Social Workflows
Executive Reporting, Roadmaps, and Social Governance Maturity
prerequisites: This advanced programme assumes you already manage one or more social channels for an organisation and understand core digital marketing concepts such as funnels, basic campaign metrics (reach, clicks, conversions), and content planning. You should be comfortable using at least one social media management or analytics tool (for example, native platform insights, Hootsuite, or Sprout Social) and working with spreadsheets. No coding is required. All advanced topics such as AI-supported workflows, attribution, and automation are taught at an operational application level so you can brief, configure, and govern them, not engineer them from scratch.
